newsitem.title: FRANCE: French Gaullist senator probed for sleaze.
newsitem.headline: French Gaullist senator probed for sleaze.

text.p: A French judge has formally placed a ruling Gaullist party senator and his wife under investigation on suspicion that she was paid out of public funds for a job that did not exist, judicial sources said on Tuesday.

Marie-Aline Dugoin is suspected of receiving a monthly salary of 23,000 francs ($4,000) for two years for a fictitious job at the Essone regional authority, near Paris, which her husband Xavier heads.

The probe, for misuse of public funds, is an embarrassing blow to the ruling centre-right five days ahead of elections to the National Assembly (lower house), even though Dugoin, a member of the upper house, is not running.
Xavier Dugoin is also being investigated in another case involving Paris mayor Jean Tiberi, a case opposition Socialists have used in their election campaign to attack the Gaullists.

Tiberi and his wife Xaviere are under investigation for alleged misuse of public funds over a 200,000 franc ($35,000) payment she received from the Essonne authority for a report largely copied out of a book.
Being placed under investigation may, but does not automatically, lead to trial.
The Dugoins have made no public comment on accusations against them. Tiberi and his wife have consistently denied any wrongdoing.
